title: Novel furfural-complexed approach to synthesizing carbon-Doped ZnO with breakthrough photocatalytic efficacy.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Methods A series of C-Z variants (C-Z-1 to C-Z-5) and an undoped sample (ZnO-0) were synthesized. The influence of furfural on the synthesis process and doping mechanism was analyzed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and UV–visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS).

sections.heading: Simplified synthesis of C-Z nanostructures
sections.text: Simplified synthesis of C-Z nanostructures The fabrication of C-Z nanostructures is a pioneering and simplified method that does not require surfactants, pH adjustment, centrifugation, or hazardous chemicals. This novel approach demands only two precursor substances: zinc nitrate hexahydrate (Zn(NO 3 ) 2 ·6H 2 O) and the organic compound furfural (C 4 H 3 OCHO). The procedure began by manually blending the precursors in a mortar using a pestle for approximately 10 min to obtain a homogenous mixture. During manual grinding, complexation occurs between inorganic zinc and organic carbon-based molecules, setting the stage for the subsequent synthesis of C-ZnO nanoparticles. Upon heating the resultant mixture in a quartz tube furnace at approximately 500 °C under a nitrogen atmosphere, the thermal degradation of furfural uniformly distributes carbon within the zinc oxide matrix. Remarkably, furfural fulfills a dual purpose in this synthetic route: it acts as a carbon source for doping, enhancing the photocatalytic efficacy of ZnO, and concurrently impeding the agglomeration of the nanoparticles, thus yielding a uniform nanostructured material. Adjusting the furfural volume (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 1.0 mL) allowed the fine-tuning of the carbon levels in ZnO, denoted as C-Z-1 to C-Z-5, respectively. This gradation of carbon content is instrumental in systematically exploring its influence on the photocatalytic activity of the material. For benchmarking purposes, a pristine ZnO reference sample (ZnO-0) was synthesized under identical conditions but without furfural. The innovation of this methodology lies in its minimalism and eco-friendliness, potentially revolutionizing the production of carbon-doped nanostructures by providing an accessible, low-cost, and scalable alternative to traditional nanoparticle-doping techniques. This has significant implications for sustainable material development, particularly for applications in environmental remediation and solar-energy harnessing.
